# Green Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and deteriorating public services, promising a "fairer, greener country" through ambitious investment and systemic reform.

## Key Policy Areas

### Health & Social Care
The NHS requires £28bn additional annual spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Priorities include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, restoring NHS dentistry (£3bn annually by 2030), and introducing free personal care. Mental health services would receive equal footing with physical health, with counsellors in every school.

### Housing
The party pledges 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A £29bn five-year programme would retrofit homes for energy efficiency.

### Energy & Climate
Plans include achieving 70% wind-powered electricity by 2030, banning new fossil fuel extraction, introducing a carbon tax starting at £120/tonne, and bringing water companies and energy retailers into public ownership. Nuclear power would be phased out.

### Economy & Work
A £40bn annual green investment programme would transform the economy. Workers would benefit from a £15 minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, restored union rights, and movement toward a four-day week. Universal Credit would increase by £40 weekly, and the two-child benefit cap would be abolished.

### Education
Proposals include scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, £8bn school investment, free school meals for all children, and abolishing Ofsted. Academies would return to local authority control.

### Transport
Public transport subsidies would reach £10bn annually, with railways renationalised, free bus travel for under-18s, and £2.5bn yearly for cycling and walking infrastructure. Petrol and diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

### Environment
A Rights of Nature Act would give nature legal personhood. Targets include protecting 30% of land and sea by 2030, rewetting peatlands, and increasing woodland by 50%.

### Democracy & Rights
Reforms include proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords, and defending human rights legislation. The hostile immigration environment would end, with safe asylum routes established.

### International
The party supports an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian state recognition, rejoining the EU, signing the UN nuclear weapons prohibition treaty, and increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI.

## Funding
Revenue would come from wealth taxes on assets over £10m, aligned capital gains taxation, a carbon tax, and business tax reforms—estimated to raise £50-70bn annually by parliament's end.
